A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyGPrompt despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; corresponding methods and experiments can be matched across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original node-classification and link-prediction experiments, component ablations, backbone comparisons, sensitivity analysis, and data-abundant results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v6 reports original experiments on four datasets, including Genre, together with component ablations, expanded backbone comparisons, and sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: The historical-neighbor time input changes from elapsed time t−t′ to timestamp t′ in Equation 2 and the prompted encoder equation, v4 Equation 11 versus v6 Equation 10. This changes the written computational specification, although implementation changes are not documented. Dual prompts, condition-nets, losses, and frozen-backbone tuning otherwise match after feature-to-node renaming.

E1.justification: v6 adds Genre to node classification and both link-prediction settings in Table 1. This introduces music-listening interactions and 474-class preference labels over 1,500 days, substantially extending the three binary-label, 30-day user–post/course datasets retained from v4.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GraphMixer and ProG and removes DyRep and JODIE from that comparison, although both remain in Table 3. Table 3 additionally compares TREND and GraphMixer with their DyGPrompt adaptations. These changes materially broaden and revise the evaluated comparator suite.

E3.justification: Node classification changes from reported accuracy to AUC-ROC in Section 5.1 and associated displays; unchanged shared scores do not establish reevaluation. v4's data-abundant protocol using 1% training and 1% validation data disappears. Figure 4 extends the displayed alpha range from 2–128 to 1–128. The main chronological split and 30-event adaptation protocol remain.

E4.justification: v4 Appendix E/Table 5, testing whether performance persists with more downstream training data, is removed. Conversely, backbone generality analysis expands from four architectures to six, adding TREND and GraphMixer, and alpha sensitivity extends to 1. The six component-ablation variants and class-embedding visualization remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 sampled tasks, five random seeds per task, and means and standard deviations over 500 results. The new Table 1 entries follow the same reporting practice; no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure or increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: v6 adds Genre, GraphMixer/ProG, and additional backbone results while removing all data-abundant Table 5 results. Existing entries also change: Table 2's Variant 1 Wikipedia transductive AUC changes from 69.05 to 55.78, and Variant 2 from 66.51 to 68.12. Shared Table 1 scores remain numerically unchanged, but the classification metric revision prevents treating them as verified same-metric comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a limited computational-complexity derivation absent from v4. It combines encoder cost O(d^L · |V|) with prompting cost O((K + 2) · (|V| + 1)) and argues that encoding dominates the total cost.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: dual prompts bridge task and temporal gaps, dual condition-nets capture mutually conditioned node–time patterns, and DyGPrompt outperforms competing approaches. Four rather than three benchmarks expands supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v6 adds explanations attributing weak TGAT/TGN results to scarce recent adaptation data and smaller MOOC ablation differences to less dynamic interactions. It also explains node prompts' usefulness for link prediction through distributional differences and argues that prompting overhead is minimal. v4's explicit limitation concerning the absence of static-graph pre-training is removed.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 newly documents the tuning procedure and explicitly specifies averaging class prototypes. The appendices add Genre statistics and a data-access pointer, plus TREND, GraphMixer, and ProG implementation descriptions. DyRep/JODIE implementation details disappear despite retained backbone tests. Optimizer, hardware, and the stated DyGPrompt condition-net dimensions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 adds a connection to hypernetworks, cites additional application and few-shot/cold-start research, and replaces several introductory references. It more precisely distinguishes existing node-specific prompts and TIGPrompt from mutual node–time conditioning. The overall positioning around dynamic graph learning, pre-training, and graph prompting remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled 'Node-Time Conditional Prompt Learning in Dynamic Graphs,' with systematic feature-to-node terminology changes. The introduction, scope, related work, and experimental discussion receive extensive rewriting. Backbone and hyperparameter sections are merged, appendices are reorganized, and citations change from numbered to author–year format.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from nine to twelve dataset/task columns, Table 3 expands to six backbones, and Table 4 adds Genre. Algorithm 1 is introduced and Table 5 removed. Figure 2 is relabeled and redrawn, Figure 4 changes colors, axes, and range, and the document adopts different headers, typography, and display placement.

improvement.justification: v6 adds useful comparator coverage, backbone tests, and procedural documentation, but removes data-abundant evidence and explicit limitations. Its accuracy-to-AUC-ROC revision is unexplained despite identical shared classification scores. Additionally, Genre has 474 classes in Table 4, while the stated 30-event sampling rule requires at least one user per class, with no exception described. These unresolved evaluation issues prevent confidently determining whether the additions yield a net quality improvement.
